_**Total War: Three Kingdoms**_ is a [turn-based strategy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turn-based_strategy "Turn-based strategy")[real-time tactics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real-time_tactics "Real-time tactics")[video game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_game "Video game") developed by [Creative Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Creative_Assembly "Creative Assembly") and published by [Sega](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sega "Sega"). As the 12th mainline entry (the 13th entry) in the _[Total War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total\_War\_(video\_game\_series) "Total War (video game series)")_ series, the game was released for [Windows](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windows "Windows") on May 23, 2019. [Feral Interactive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feral_Interactive "Feral Interactive") released a [Linux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linux "Linux") and [macOS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MacOS "MacOS") version of the game on the same day.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_War:_Three_Kingdoms#cite_note-1)

## Gameplay

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Total_War:_Three_Kingdoms&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Gameplay")]

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/d/d4/Total_War_Three_Kingdoms_screenshot.jpg/250px-Total_War_Three_Kingdoms_screenshot.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Total_War_Three_Kingdoms_screenshot.jpg)

In _Total War: Three Kingdoms_, generals can engage in a one-versus-one [dueling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dueling "Dueling"), which ends when one of them dies or flees.

Like its predecessors, _Total War: Three Kingdoms_ is a [turn-based strategy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turn-based_strategy "Turn-based strategy")[real-time tactics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real-time_tactics "Real-time tactics") game. Set during the [End of the Han dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/End_of_the_Han_dynasty "End of the Han dynasty") (189-220) and into the [Three Kingdoms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Three_Kingdoms "Three Kingdoms") era (220–280), the player controls one of the factions, who must eliminate or vassalize other factions, gaining enough prestige to declare themselves Emperor. The player must also defeat the other two Emperors which are the two most powerful factions, unify [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China "China") and become its ultimate ruler.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_War:_Three_Kingdoms#cite_note-2) These factions are led by warlords, such as [Cao Cao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cao_Cao "Cao Cao"), [Liu Bei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liu_Bei "Liu Bei"), and [Sun Quan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sun_Quan "Sun Quan").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_War:_Three_Kingdoms#cite_note-3) In siege battles, the player commands both infantry and cavalry units. All the units featured in the game are divided into different [retinues](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retinue "Retinue"), with each led by a powerful general. The player can deploy up to three generals into the battlefield at once along with three in reserve, and there will only be access to the units that those generals can recruit.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_War:_Three_Kingdoms#cite_note-4)

The player wins a siege battle when all hostile generals are killed or the central point of the city is captured. These generals, which can be commanded separately from their troops, have the possession of unique ancillaries, that can be looted once they are killed. For instance, [Lü Bu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L%C3%BC_Bu "Lü Bu")'s [Red Hare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Hare "Red Hare") can be captured and used by other generals. Generals can engage in a one-versus-one [dueling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dueling "Dueling"), which ends when one of them dies or flees. Each general has different classes and specialties, granting their units with both active and passive buffs.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_War:_Three_Kingdoms#cite_note-5) The team introduces the concept of "[guanxi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guanxi "Guanxi")" to the game, in which each general will form social connections and relationships with other characters. Viewing concepts like "obligations, reciprocity, and trust" as important virtues, these generals have unique personalities and desires that the player needs to cater to. If their demands are not met, their happiness rating will drop and this may lead to various repercussions.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_War:_Three_Kingdoms#cite_note-guanxi-6) Unlike previous _Total War_ games where characters rarely interact with each other, the generals featured in the game are actively forming relationships with the people they meet throughout the campaign. This adds a strategic layer to the game in which players need to understand these generals before making any decisions.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_War:_Three_Kingdoms#cite_note-guanxi-6)

The game features two modes. The first mode, "Romance", is based on the novel _[Romance of the Three Kingdoms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romance\_of\_the\_Three\_Kingdoms "Romance of the Three Kingdoms")_, in which generals are gifted with nearly superhuman strength. Another mode, "Records", based on _[Records of the Three Kingdoms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Records\_of\_the\_Three\_Kingdoms "Records of the Three Kingdoms")_, presents a more historically authentic version. In Records, the generals have their powers removed and they can no longer be commanded separately, in addition to changing certain equipment in-game to be more historically authentic.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_War:_Three_Kingdoms#cite_note-7)

## Plot

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Total_War:_Three_Kingdoms&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Plot")]

Taking place in 190 AD, the once glorious [Han dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_dynasty "Han dynasty") is on the verge of collapse. The new emperor, [Emperor Xian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emperor_Xian_of_Han "Emperor Xian of Han"), enthroned at the age of eight, was manipulated by the warlord [Dong Zhuo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dong_Zhuo "Dong Zhuo"), whose oppressive rule leads to chaos. New warlords rise and form alliances to start the [campaign against Dong Zhuo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Campaign_against_Dong_Zhuo "Campaign against Dong Zhuo"). With each warlord having personal ambitions and allegiances constantly shifting, the champions that emerge from the everlasting wars will shape the future of China.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_War:_Three_Kingdoms#cite_note-premise-8)

## Development and release

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Total_War:_Three_Kingdoms&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Development and release")]

The game was developed by [Creative Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Creative_Assembly "Creative Assembly"). Creative Assembly had refined many elements of the game, bringing changes to both the [artificial intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence "Artificial intelligence") and the [user interface](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User_interface "User interface"). The team introduced the system of "guanxi" in order to make the characters and generals more important in the game, as _Records_ and _Romances_, two of the team's most prominent source materials, have a huge focus on characters. The [sinologist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinology "Sinology")[Rafe de Crespigny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rafe_de_Crespigny "Rafe de Crespigny"), an expert on the era, acted as a consultant for the game.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_War:_Three_Kingdoms#cite_note-9)

When the game was still in preproduction in November 2016, Creative Assembly announced that the next historical _Total War_ title would explore a new era instead of being a sequel to any prior game.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_War:_Three_Kingdoms#cite_note-10)_Three Kingdoms_ was revealed by publisher [Sega](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sega "Sega") on January 11, 2018 with a cinematic trailer.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_War:_Three_Kingdoms#cite_note-premise-8) Originally set to be released in the second half of 2018, the game was delayed to early 2019 so that the team had additional development time to complete the production.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_War:_Three_Kingdoms#cite_note-11) A new release date of March 7, 2019 was later announced, which was then delayed to May 23, 2019.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_War:_Three_Kingdoms#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_War:_Three_Kingdoms#cite_note-13)

_Total War: Three Kingdoms_ received positive reviews from critics, with many specifically praising the character-driven gameplay mechanics and storytelling elements. Chris Wray of wccftech describes the game is "as close to flawless, with a fantastic balance of [4X](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/4X "4X") strategy and character-focused development and emergent storytelling."[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_War:_Three_Kingdoms#cite_note-30)_[IGN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IGN "IGN")_'s TJ Hafer stated that _Three Kingdoms_ should serve as the example for all games of its genre going forward.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_War:_Three_Kingdoms#cite_note-ignreview-23) Edwin Evans-Thirlwell of _[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Guardian "The Guardian")_ stated the game "...is a wonderfully torrid period epic that understands the greatest stories are written about people, not empires."[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_War:_Three_Kingdoms#cite_note-Guardian-26) Jody Macgregor of _[PC Gamer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PC\_Gamer "PC Gamer")_ praised the campaign elements, but found the game still could not break off from longstanding problems the series has always faced, claiming _Three Kingdoms_ "is not the best Total War game but not the worst by a long shot."[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_War:_Three_Kingdoms#cite_note-PCGUS-24)

The Romance mode has also been praised as bringing fascinating additions to the game, with many reviewers comparing it to _[Total War: Warhammer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total\_War:\_Warhammer "Total War: Warhammer")_. Preston Dozsa of _CGMagazine_ stated that the game "represents the best of both the historical and fantasy sides of the franchise."[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_War:_Three_Kingdoms#cite_note-31) Sean Martin from Hooked Gamers stated the game "is the most divergent _Total War_ I’ve seen since _Total War: Warhammer._.. taking what is good in fantasy and using it to complement the historical components of the game."[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_War:_Three_Kingdoms#cite_note-32) Denis Ryan of _[Rock, Paper, Shotgun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock,\_Paper,\_Shotgun "Rock, Paper, Shotgun")_ said it draws inspiration from many games that [Creative Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Creative_Assembly "Creative Assembly") developed in the past, and "despite the resemblance there really is no game which has quite the same combination of elements, nor is there any strategy game that looks this good."[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_War:_Three_Kingdoms#cite_note-RPS-28)

Chris Tapsell of _[Eurogamer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurogamer "Eurogamer")_ also stated that the game is "ambitious and sometimes overwhelming."[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_War:_Three_Kingdoms#cite_note-EuroG-20)_[PCGamesN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PCGamesN "PCGamesN")_'s Phil Iwaniuk said the game brings issues along with innovations, and noted that despite the memorable campaign, the real-time battles portion lacks depth compared to rest of the series.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_War:_Three_Kingdoms#cite_note-PCGN-25)

Beifang Lin of _GamerSky_, a Chinese publication, commended the development team for their professionalism and deep understanding of the historical era, concluding that the Three Kingdoms theme was well integrated into the _Total War_ system.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_War:_Three_Kingdoms#cite_note-gskyreview-27)

### Sales

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Total_War:_Three_Kingdoms&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Sales")]

According to the developer Creative Assembly, _Total War: Three Kingdoms_ was the most pre-ordered _[Total War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total\_War\_(video\_game\_series) "Total War (video game series)")_ game until its release date.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_War:_Three_Kingdoms#cite_note-PCGN_sale-33) The game also set the record of concurrent players for _Total War_ series, with over 160,000 people playing simultaneously on the day of release and reaching 192,000 by the first weekend. This made it the largest concurrent played strategy game on Steam.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_War:_Three_Kingdoms#cite_note-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_War:_Three_Kingdoms#cite_note-Pcgamer_sale-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_War:_Three_Kingdoms#cite_note-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_War:_Three_Kingdoms#cite_note-37) It became the fastest-selling game in the history of the franchise, selling one million copies in a week since its initial release[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_War:_Three_Kingdoms#cite_note-38) and amassed a total of 3,210,000 units sold as of March 2025.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_War:_Three_Kingdoms#cite_note-39)

The **Yellow Turban Rebellion** (Chinese: 黃巾之亂; pinyin: Huángjīn zhī luàn), alternatively translated as the **Yellow Scarves Rebellion**, was a [peasant revolt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_peasant_revolts "List of peasant revolts") during the late [Eastern Han dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Han_dynasty "Eastern Han dynasty") of [ancient China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_China "Ancient China"). The uprising broke out in 184 AD, during the reign of [Emperor Ling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emperor_Ling_of_Han "Emperor Ling of Han"). Although the main rebellion was suppressed by 185 AD, it took 21 years to fully subdue resisting areas and emerging rebellions, which was only achieved in 205 AD.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-Smitha_2015-1) The weakening of the imperial court and the rising political influence of autonomous regional military-governors, who helped suppress the rebellion, eventually led to rampant [warlord](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warlord "Warlord") dominance and the resultant [Three Kingdoms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Three_Kingdoms "Three Kingdoms") period.

The rebellion, which took its name from the colour of the rebels' headwear (巾 _jīn_, defined as more of a [scarf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scarf "Scarf")[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-5) than a [turban](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turban "Turban")) marked an important point in the [history of Taoism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Taoism "History of Taoism") due to the rebel leaders' association with the then secret [Taoist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taoism "Taoism") societies.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-6) The revolt was also used as the inciting event in the 14th-century historical novel _[Romance of the Three Kingdoms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romance\_of\_the\_Three\_Kingdoms "Romance of the Three Kingdoms")_.

## Background

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Yellow_Turban_Rebellion&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background")]

Further information: [History of the Han dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_Han_dynasty "History of the Han dynasty") and [Society and culture of the Han dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Society_and_culture_of_the_Han_dynasty "Society and culture of the Han dynasty")

By 184 AD, the Han Dynasty's central government was weakened by court [eunuchs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eunuch "Eunuch") abusing their power over the emperor to enrich themselves. Twelve of the most powerful eunuchs were referred to as the [Ten Attendants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ten_Attendants "Ten Attendants") with [Emperor Ling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emperor_Ling_of_Han "Emperor Ling of Han") once claiming that "Regular Attendant Zhang Rang is my father and Regular Attendant Zhao Zhong is my mother".[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-:0-7) The government corruption was perceived as causing plagues, natural disasters, and poor agricultural yields, reflecting that the emperor had lost his [Mandate of Heaven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandate_of_Heaven "Mandate of Heaven").

As flooding along the [Yellow River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_River "Yellow River") forced farmers and military settlers south, the labor surplus incentivized exploitation. Disease outbreaks were reported in 171, 173, 179, 182, and 185 AD, with the potential cause theorized as the [Antonine Plague](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonine_Plague "Antonine Plague") of 165 to 181CE of [smallpox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smallpox "Smallpox") or [measles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Measles "Measles") spreading along the [Silk Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silk_Road "Silk Road").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-:0-7)

Through claims of providing curative water and bamboo playing, the Taoist leader [Zhang Jue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhang_Jue "Zhang Jue") developed his initial following to send his disciples throughout northern China in preparation for a revolt.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-:0-7) Their rapid rise was relatively unnoticed until they became too powerful to challenge.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-ANU-8) Zhang Jue intended to launch an uprising throughout the Han Empire, but the plan was betrayed before he was ready. Rebel sympathizers in [Luoyang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luoyang "Luoyang") were arrested and executed, forcing a premature beginning in March 184. Despite the inevitable lack of co-ordination and overall preparation, tens of thousands of men rose in rebellion. Government offices were plundered and destroyed and the imperial armies were immediately forced on the defensive.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-ANU-8)

## Rebels

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Yellow_Turban_Rebellion&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Rebels")]

The rebellion was led by [Zhang Jue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhang_Jue "Zhang Jue") (also referred to as Zhang Jiao, known to his followers as the "General of Heaven") and his two younger brothers Zhang Bao (張寶) and Zhang Liang (張梁), who were born in [Julu Commandery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julu_Commandery "Julu Commandery"). The brothers had founded a Taoist religious sect in present-day [Shandong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shandong "Shandong"), praised as healers who offered free care to impoverished patients. Recognizing how the local government abused the peasant class through harsh labor and heavy taxes, they plotted rebellion.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### Taoist sect

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Yellow_Turban_Rebellion&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Taoist sect")]

The rebels were the first followers of the Way of Supreme Peace (太平道; _Tàipíng Dào_) and venerated the deity [Huang–Lao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huang%E2%80%93Lao "Huang–Lao"), who according to Zhang Jue, had given him a sacred book called the _Crucial Keys to the Way of Peace_ (太平要術; _Tàipíng Yàoshù_) based on the _[Taipingjing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taipingjing "Taipingjing")_. Zhang Jue, who was said to be a sorcerer, called himself the "Great Teacher" (大賢良師). When the rebellion was proclaimed on 4 March, Zhang Jue created a 16-word slogan spread through the brothers' medical work:[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-HHS_71_Yellow_Turban_Rebellion-9)

> The Azure Sky[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-10) is already dead; the Yellow Sky[[c]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-11) will soon rise.  
> When the year is _[jiǎzǐ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese\_calendar "Chinese calendar")_,[[d]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-12) there will be prosperity [under Heaven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tianxia "Tianxia")!  
> (蒼天已死，黃天當立。歲在甲子，天下大吉。)

### Religious practices

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Yellow_Turban_Rebellion&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Religious practices")]

Zhang Jue claimed to cure patients by having them confess sins for Taoist [faith healing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faith_healing "Faith healing"). The Zhang brothers believed in an impending apocalyptic change in the _[jiazi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese\_calendar "Chinese calendar")_ year, the beginning of the new [sexagenary cycle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexagenary_cycle "Sexagenary cycle"), involving yellow skies marking new governance, which inspired the color of their headwear.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-ANU-8) Through the sect's communal activities like trances, fasting, musical performances, chanting, incense burning, and sermons, followers united across ethnic and gender lines. Several [Xiongnu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xiongnu "Xiongnu") leaders, such as [Yufuluo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chizhi_Shizhu_Hou "Chizhi Shizhu Hou"), lent their support, potentially inspiring Zhang Jue to adopt their [shamanistic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shamanism "Shamanism") beliefs.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-13)

Despite few surviving records, the early Path of Supreme Peace was likely similar to the [Way of the Celestial Masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Way_of_the_Celestial_Masters "Way of the Celestial Masters"), considering that Zhang Jue claimed to be a descendant of [Zhang Daoling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhang_Daoling "Zhang Daoling"). Much of the _[Taipingjing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taipingjing "Taipingjing")'s_ surviving 52 chapters, found in the _[Daozang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daozang "Daozang")_, have a direct relationship to the Way of the Celestial Masters with discrepancies potentially suppressed by later Taoists.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-14)

## Zhang Jue's plans for rebellion

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Yellow_Turban_Rebellion&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Zhang Jue's plans for rebellion")]

About a month before the rebellion, Zhang Jue ordered one of his advisors, Ma Yuanyi (馬元義) to recruit followers from both [Jing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jingzhou_(ancient_China) "Jingzhou (ancient China)") and [Yang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yangzhou_(ancient_China) "Yangzhou (ancient China)") provinces and have them gather in [Ye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ye_(Hebei) "Ye (Hebei)") (present-day [Linzhang County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linzhang_County "Linzhang County"), [Handan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Handan "Handan"), [Hebei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hebei "Hebei") and [Anyang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anyang "Anyang"), [Henan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henan "Henan")). Since Ma Yuanyi frequently made visits to the Han imperial capital of [Luoyang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luoyang "Luoyang") (present-day Luoyang, Henan), he was able to persuade Feng Xu (封諝) and XU Feng (徐奉), two members of Emperor Ling's trusted [eunuch faction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ten_Attendants "Ten Attendants"), to secretly aid Zhang Jue while feigning loyalty to the Emperor. However, a few days before the rebellion was set to begin, the Yellow Turbans were suddenly betrayed. One of the Taiping Dao's founding members, Tang Zhou (唐周), was excluded from further planning for reasons unknown, so he reported Ma Yuanyi to the proper authorities. Ma Yuanyi was later arrested and subsequently executed by dismemberment in Luoyang not too long after.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-Ma_Yuanyi_and_Tang_Zhou-15)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-ANU-8)

When Emperor Ling was notified of what Zhang Jue and the Taiping Dao was plotting, he ordered Zhou Bin (周斌), Prefect of the Palace Parks (鉤盾令), to conduct an investigation and capture any co-conspirators that sided with Zhang Jue. Hundreds of people were arrested and executed during this time.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-Zhou_Bin-16)

## Yellow Rebellion

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Yellow_Turban_Rebellion&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Yellow Rebellion")]

When Zhang Jue heard that the Han government had learned about his plans to rebel, he quickly sent messengers to contact his allies throughout China and take action immediately. In March, Zhang Jue started the Yellow Turban Rebellion with roughly 360,000 followers wearing yellow headscarves or turbans.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-HHS_8_Zhang_Jue-17) He called himself the "Lord General of Heaven" (天公將軍), while his brothers Zhang Bao and Zhang Liang were called the "Lord General of Earth" (地公將軍) and "Lord General of Man" (人公將軍), respectively. The rebels attacked government offices, pillaged villages, and seized control of commanderies. Within 10 days, the rebellion had spread throughout China, alarming the Han imperial court in [Luoyang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luoyang "Luoyang").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-Heaven,_Earth,_People_Generals-18)

The rebels were mostly concentrated in the [Ji](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ji_Province "Ji Province"), [Jing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jing_Province "Jing Province"), [You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You_Province "You Province") and [Yu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yuzhou_(ancient_China) "Yuzhou (ancient China)") provinces. The group led by Zhang Jue and his brothers gained their support in Ji Province, located just north of the [Yellow River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_River "Yellow River"), near Zhang Jue's home territory of [Julu Commandery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julu_Commandery "Julu Commandery") (around present-day [Pingxiang County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pingxiang_County "Pingxiang County"), [Hebei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hebei "Hebei")) and [Wei Commandery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wei_Commandery "Wei Commandery") (around present-day [Handan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Handan "Handan"), Hebei). A second major uprising took place in [Guangyang Commandery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangyang_Commandery "Guangyang Commandery") (around present-day [Beijing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beijing "Beijing")) and [Zhuo Commandery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhuo_Commandery "Zhuo Commandery") (around present-day [Zhuozhou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhuozhou "Zhuozhou"), Hebei) in You Province. The third centre of the rebellion was in [Yingchuan Commandery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yingchuan_Commandery "Yingchuan Commandery") (around present-day [Xuchang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xuchang "Xuchang"), [Henan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henan "Henan")) and [Runan Commandery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Runan_Commandery "Runan Commandery") (around present-day [Xinyang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xinyang "Xinyang"), Henan) in Yu Province, and [Nanyang Commandery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanyang_Commandery "Nanyang Commandery") (around present-day [Nanyang, Henan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanyang,_Henan "Nanyang, Henan")) in northern [Jing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chu_(state) "Chu (state)") Province.

On 1 April 184, Emperor Ling appointed his brother-in-law [He Jin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/He_Jin "He Jin"), the Intendant of Henan (河南尹), as General-in-Chief (大將軍) and ordered him to supervise the imperial armies in suppressing the rebellion.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-He_Jin-19) Emperor Ling also appointed three generals – [Lu Zhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lu_Zhi_(Han_dynasty) "Lu Zhi (Han dynasty)"), [Huangfu Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huangfu_Song "Huangfu Song") and [Zhu Jun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhu_Jun_(Han_dynasty) "Zhu Jun (Han dynasty)") – to lead three separate armies to deal with the rebels with a total of roughly 40,000 troops.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-HHS_71_Huangfu_Song_and_Zhu_Jun-20) Lu Zhi went for Zhang Jue's base in Ji Province, while Huangfu Song and Zhu Jun headed to Yingchuan Commandery.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-HHS_8_Lu_Zhi,_Huangfu_Song,_Zhu_Jun-21)

### You Province: Guangyang and Zhuo commanderies

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Yellow_Turban_Rebellion&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: You Province: Guangyang and Zhuo commanderies")]

In [You Province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You_Province "You Province"), the rebels killed Guo Xun (郭勳), the provincial Inspector, and Liu Wei (劉衛), the Administrator of Guangyang Commandery.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-Guo_Xun_and_Liu_Wei-22)

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/df/Three_Brothers_during_the_Yellow_Turban_Rebellion.jpg/250px-Three_Brothers_during_the_Yellow_Turban_Rebellion.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Three_Brothers_during_the_Yellow_Turban_Rebellion.jpg)

A [Qing dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qing_dynasty "Qing dynasty") illustration of Liu Bei, Guan Yu, and Zhang Fei in 184 during the rebellion

[Zou Jing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zou_Jing_(Eastern_Han) "Zou Jing (Eastern Han)"), a colonel, led imperial forces to eliminate the rebels in You Province. [Liu Bei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liu_Bei "Liu Bei") led a group of volunteers[[e]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-23) to assist him so.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-Zou_Jing,_Liu_Bei-24)

### Yu Province: Runan and Yingchuan commanderies

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Yellow_Turban_Rebellion&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Yu Province: Runan and Yingchuan commanderies")]

When the rebellion first broke out in [Yu Province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yuzhou_(ancient_China) "Yuzhou (ancient China)"), the Han imperial court specially selected [Wang Yun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wang_Yun_(Han_dynasty) "Wang Yun (Han dynasty)") to be the inspector of the province to oversee the military operations.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-HHS_66_Wang_Yun-25)

Zhao Qian (趙謙), the administrator of [Runan Commandery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Runan_Commandery "Runan Commandery"), led his troops to attack the rebels before [Zhu Jun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhu_Jun_(Han_dynasty) "Zhu Jun (Han dynasty)") arrived, but was defeated at Shaoling (邵陵; in present-day southeastern Henan).[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-HHS_8_Zhao_Qian-26) When Chen County (陳縣; present-day [Huaiyang County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huaiyang_County "Huaiyang County"), Henan) was under attack by the rebels, seven of Zhao Qian's subordinates, who were non-military personnel, armed themselves with swords and attempted to fight the rebels but were all killed. Later, after the rebellion was suppressed, [Emperor Ling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emperor_Ling_of_Han "Emperor Ling of Han") issued an edict to honor the seven as the "Seven Virtuous" (七賢).[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-Seven_Virtuous-27)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-Xie_Cheng,_'Seven_Virtuous'-28)

[Chen State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chen_Commandery "Chen Commandery") (陳國; around present-day [Zhoukou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhoukou "Zhoukou"), Henan), one of the commanderies in Yu Province, avoided the Yellow Turban Rebellion's bloodshed because the rebels feared Prince [Liu Chong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liu_Chong_(Prince_Min_of_Chen) "Liu Chong (Prince Min of Chen)"), famous for his unit of skilled archers.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-HHS_76_Liu_Chong-29)

The rebels in Runan Commandery, led by Bo Cai (波才), initially defeated Zhu Jun in battle and drove him back. The imperial court sent a cavalry contingent, led by young officer [Cao Cao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cao_Cao "Cao Cao") (曹操), as reinforcements for Zhu Jun.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-HHS_71_Cao_Cao-30) Sometime between 28 May and 25 June, Zhu Jun, [Huangfu Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huangfu_Song "Huangfu Song"), and Cao Cao joined forces to defeat Bo Cai at Changshe (長社; east of present-day [Changge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Changge "Changge"), Henan).[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-31)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-HHS_71_Huangfu_Song_vs_Bo_Cai-32) While Bo Cai attempted to flee, Huangfu Song and Zhu Jun pursued him to Yangzhai County (陽翟縣; present-day [Yuzhou, Henan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yuzhou,_Henan "Yuzhou, Henan")) and defeated him again, causing the rebels to scatter.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-Bo_Cai_and_Peng_Tuo-33)

Huangfu Song and Zhu Jun then defeated the rebels in Runan Commandery, led by Peng Tuo (彭脫), at Xihua County (西華縣; south of present-day [Xihua County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xihua_County "Xihua County"), Henan).[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-Bo_Cai_and_Peng_Tuo-33) The imperial court ordered them to split up: Huangfu Song would attack the rebels at [Dong Commandery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dong_Commandery "Dong Commandery") (東郡; around present-day [Puyang County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puyang_County "Puyang County"), Henan), while Zhu Jun would attack the rebels at Nanyang Commandery.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-HHS_8_Huangfu_Song_and_Zhu_Jun-34) During this time, [Wang Yun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wang_Yun_(Han_dynasty) "Wang Yun (Han dynasty)"), the Inspector of [Yu Province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yuzhou_(ancient_China) "Yuzhou (ancient China)"), found evidence that the rebels had been secretly maintaining contact with Zhang Rang (張讓), the leader of the [eunuch faction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ten_Attendants "Ten Attendants") in Luoyang, so he reported it to Emperor Ling, who scolded Zhang Rang but did not punish him.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-HHS_66_Wang_Yun-25)

Between 7 November and 6 December, Bao Hong (鮑鴻), a colonel, led imperial forces to attack the rebels in Gebei (葛陂; northwest of present-day [Xincai County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xincai_County "Xincai County"), Henan) and defeated them.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-ReferenceA-35)

### Ji Province: Wei and Julu commanderies

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Yellow_Turban_Rebellion&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Ji Province: Wei and Julu commanderies")]

In the meantime, [Lu Zhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lu_Zhi_(Han_dynasty) "Lu Zhi (Han dynasty)") defeated Zhang Jue's rebel forces in [Julu Commandery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julu_Commandery "Julu Commandery") and besieged the rebel leader in Guangzong County (廣宗縣; southeast of present-day [Guangzong County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzong_County "Guangzong County"), Hebei). However, after a eunuch falsely accused Lu Zhi of treason, [Emperor Ling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emperor_Ling_of_Han "Emperor Ling of Han") ordered his arrest, escorted back to [Luoyang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luoyang "Luoyang") as a prisoner.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-Lu_Zhi-36) The imperial court then sent General [Dong Zhuo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dong_Zhuo "Dong Zhuo") to take over Lu Zhi's position and attack Zhang Jue. However, Dong Zhuo failed and retreated.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-HHS_8_Dong_Zhuo-37)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-HHS_71_Dong_Zhuo-38)

On 23 or 24 September, [Huangfu Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huangfu_Song "Huangfu Song") and [Fu Xie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fu_Xie?action=edit&redlink=1 "Fu Xie (page does not exist)") (傅燮), a Major under him,[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-Fu_Xie-39) defeated the rebels at Cangting (倉亭; north of present-day [Yanggu County, Shandong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yanggu_County,_Shandong "Yanggu County, Shandong")), captured their leader Bu Ji (卜己), and killed over 7,000 rebels, including other minor leaders Zhang Bo (張伯) and Liang Zhongning (梁仲寧).[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-HHS_71_Bu_Ji-40)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-Fu_Xie_defeated_Bu_Ji,_Zhang_Bo_and_Liang_Zhongning-41) On 25 September, the imperial court ordered him to replace Dong Zhuo and lead his troops north to Guangzong County and attack Zhang Jue.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-HHS_8_Huangfu_Song,_Cangting-42)

Zhang Jue died of illness in October 184 while under attack by Huangfu Song in Guangzong County. Between 21 November and 20 December, Huangfu Song kept attacking Zhang Liang, who had taken over command of his brother's followers at Guangzong County. Unable to defeat Zhang Liang's skilled Yellow Turbans, Huangfu Song switched to a defensive approach, tricking the rebels into lowering their guard for a devastating nighttime strike. Zhang Liang was killed in action alongside 30,000 rebels, while another 50,000 rebels drowned while attempting to flee across a river. Huangfu Song burnt over 30,000 carts containing rebel supplies and captured most of their family members.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-43) Huangfu Song then had Zhang Jue's body excavated and decapitated, sending his head to the imperial court in Luoyang.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-44)

In recognition of Huangfu Song's achievements, Emperor Ling promoted him to Left General of Chariots and Cavalry (左車騎將軍). Between 21 December 184 and 18 January 185, Huangfu Song joined forces with Guo Dian (郭典), the Administrator of Julu Commandery, to attack the remaining rebels led by Zhang Jue's other brother, Zhang Bao. They defeated the rebels at Xiaquyang County (下曲陽縣; west of present-day [Jinzhou, Hebei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jinzhou,_Hebei "Jinzhou, Hebei")), killed Zhang Bao, and received the surrender of over 100,000 rebels.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-HHS_8,_10-11th_months-45)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-HHS_71_Zhang_Bao,_Xiaquyang_County-46)

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/24/RTK_-_002.jpg/250px-RTK_-_002.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:RTK_-_002.jpg)

### Jing Province: Nanyang commandery

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Yellow_Turban_Rebellion&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Jing Province: Nanyang commandery")]

On 24 March 184, the rebels led by Zhang Mancheng (張曼成) killed Chu Gong (褚貢), the Administrator of [Nanyang Commandery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanyang_Commandery "Nanyang Commandery"), and occupied the commandery's capital, Wancheng (宛城; present-day [Wancheng District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wancheng_District "Wancheng District"), Nanyang, Henan).[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-Zhang_Mancheng_killed_Chu_Gong-47) Chu Gong's successor, Qin Jie (秦頡), rallied local forces in Nanyang Commandery to attack Zhang Mancheng and defeated and killed him between 26 June and 25 July,[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-Qin_Jie_defeated_Zhang_Mancheng-48)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-HHS_71_Zhu_Jun-49) before [Zhu Jun's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhu_Jun_(Han_dynasty) "Zhu Jun (Han dynasty)") reinforcements arrived.

After Zhang Mancheng's death, Zhao Hong (趙弘) became the new rebel leader in Wancheng. During or after October 184, Qin Jie and Zhu Jun combined forces with Xu Qiu (徐璆), the Inspector of [Jing Province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jing_Province "Jing Province"), to attack Wancheng with an army of about 18,000. They defeated and killed Zhao Hong.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-Zhao_Hong,_Zhu_Jun,_Xu_Qiu,_Qin_Jie-50)

Following Zhao Hong's death, Han Zhong (韓忠) and the remaining rebels seized control of Wancheng, continuing to resist imperial forces. Zhu Jun ordered his troops to pretend to attack from the southwest, while he secretly led 5,000 elite soldiers to infiltrate Wancheng from the northeast. Han Zhong retreated into the citadel and requested to surrender. Qin Jie, Xu Qiu and Zhang Chao (張超), a Major under Zhu Jun, all urged Zhu Jun to accept Han Zhong's surrender, but he refused. Zhu Jun instead pretended to lift the siege to lure Han Zhong to come out and attack. Han Zhong fell for the ruse, lost the battle, and tried to flee north while some 10,000 of his men were slaughtered by imperial forces. In desperation, Han Zhong surrendered to Zhu Jun, but Qin Jie had him executed.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-Han_Zhong,_Zhu_Jun,_Zhang_Chao,_Xu_Qiu,_Qin_Jie-51)

On 11 January 185, Zhu Jun defeated another rebel force led by Sun Xia (孫夏), who then fled towards Xi'e County (西鄂縣; north of present-day [Nanyang, Henan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanyang,_Henan "Nanyang, Henan")). Zhu Jun pursued him there, defeated him and caused the remaining rebels to disperse.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-Zhu_Jun_killed_Sun_Xia-52)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-Sun_Xia_fled_to_Xi'e-53)

### Xu and Yang provinces

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Yellow_Turban_Rebellion&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Xu and Yang provinces")]

In [Xu Province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xu_Province "Xu Province"), the provincial Inspector [Tao Qian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tao_Qian_(Han_dynasty) "Tao Qian (Han dynasty)"), with the aid of [Zang Ba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zang_Ba "Zang Ba"), managed to defeat the rebels to restore regional peace.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-HHS_73_Tao_Qian-54)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-SGZ_18_Zang_Ba-55)

[Sun Jian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sun_Jian "Sun Jian"), then a minor official serving in Xiapi County (下邳縣; south of present-day [Pizhou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pizhou "Pizhou"), [Jiangsu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jiangsu "Jiangsu")) in Xu Province, came to join Zhu Jun's army as a Major. He brought along several young men from Xiapi County and other soldiers recruited from the [Huai River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huai_River "Huai River") region.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-SGZ_46_Sun_Jian-56)

In [Yang Province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yang_Province "Yang Province"), the rebels attacked Shu County (舒縣; in present-day central [Anhui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anhui "Anhui")), a county in Lujiang Commandery (廬江郡; around present-day [Lu'an](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lu'an "Lu'an"), Anhui), and set fire to buildings. Yang Xu (羊續), the Administrator of Lujiang Commandery, successfully rallied thousands of able-bodied men aged 19 and above for countering the attack and firefighting.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-HHS_31_Yang_Xu-57)

### End of the rebellion

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Yellow_Turban_Rebellion&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: End of the rebellion")]

By the beginning of 185, the rebellion had mostly been suppressed following Zhu Jun's recapture of Wancheng in Nanyang Commandery and Huangfu Song's victories over the Zhang brothers in Ji Province. The remaining, scattered rebels were pursued by government forces in smaller military campaigns, and by mid-February 185, Emperor Ling issued a celebratory proclamation by changing his [era name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_era_name "Chinese era name") from Guanghe (光和) to Zhongping (中平; "pacification achieved").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-ANU-8)

## Resurgent Yellow Turban activities after early 185

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Yellow_Turban_Rebellion&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Resurgent Yellow Turban activities after early 185")]

Although the main Yellow Turban Rebellion ended by February 185, smaller rebellions by Yellow Turban remnants continued over the following two decades.

### White Wave Bandits

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Yellow_Turban_Rebellion&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: White Wave Bandits")]

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/df/Three_Brothers_during_the_Yellow_Turban_Rebellion.jpg/250px-Three_Brothers_during_the_Yellow_Turban_Rebellion.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Three_Brothers_during_the_Yellow_Turban_Rebellion.jpg)

Between 16 March and 13 April 188, Guo Tai (郭太) led some 100,000 Yellow Turban remnants to start a rebellion in [Xihe Commandery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xihe_Commandery "Xihe Commandery") (around present-day [Fenyang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fenyang "Fenyang"), [Shanxi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanxi "Shanxi")). As they originated from Baibo Valley (白波谷; "White Wave Valley") in Xihe Commandery, they later became known as the "White Wave Bandits" (白波賊). They allied with the [Xiongnu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xiongnu "Xiongnu") leader [Yufuluo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chizhishizhuhou_Chanyu "Chizhishizhuhou Chanyu") and attacked [Taiyuan Commandery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taiyuan_Commandery "Taiyuan Commandery") (around present-day [Taiyuan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taiyuan "Taiyuan"), [Shanxi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanxi "Shanxi")) and [Hedong Commandery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hedong_Commandery "Hedong Commandery") (around present-day [Yuncheng, Shanxi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yuncheng,_Shanxi "Yuncheng, Shanxi")).[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-HHS_8_Guo_Tai-58)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-59) Between 27 October and 25 November 189, when the bandits attacked Hedong Commandery, the warlord [Dong Zhuo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dong_Zhuo "Dong Zhuo")'s son-in-law [Niu Fu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Niu_Fu "Niu Fu") attacked the bandits but failed in the attempt.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-60)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-61)

Around mid-195, [Emperor Xian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emperor_Xian_of_Han "Emperor Xian of Han") fled from the imperial capital [Chang'an](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chang'an "Chang'an"), where he had been held hostage by Dong Zhuo's followers, led by [Li Jue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Li_Jue_(Han_dynasty) "Li Jue (Han dynasty)") and [Guo Si](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guo_Si "Guo Si"), since Dong Zhuo's death in 192. He returned to the ruins of the old imperial capital [Luoyang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luoyang "Luoyang"), which Dong Zhuo burnt down in 191 while forcefully relocating its residents to Chang'an. [Dong Cheng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dong_Cheng_(Han_dynasty) "Dong Cheng (Han dynasty)") (a former subordinate of Niu Fu) and [Yang Feng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yang_Feng "Yang Feng") (a former White Wave bandit)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-HHS_72_Yang_Feng-62) protected Emperor Xian in Luoyang when Li Jue and Guo Si tried to pursue and bring the emperor back to Chang'an. Dong Cheng and Yang Feng summoned the White Wave Bandits, led by Li Le (李樂), [Han Xian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Xian_(Han_dynasty) "Han Xian (Han dynasty)"), Hu Cai (胡才) and others, to come to Emperor Xian's aid. Xiongnu forces led by [Qubei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qubei "Qubei") also responded to the call and came to help Emperor Xian resist Li Jue and Guo Si's forces.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-HHS_72_White_Wave_Bandits-63) Between 195 and 196, the warlord [Cao Cao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cao_Cao "Cao Cao") led his forces into Luoyang and escorted Emperor Xian to his own base in Xu (許; present-day [Xuchang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xuchang "Xuchang"), [Henan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henan "Henan")) and established the new imperial capital there.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### Yi Province: Ma Xiang and Zhao Zhi

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Yellow_Turban_Rebellion&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Yi Province: Ma Xiang and Zhao Zhi")]

In 188, [Ma Xiang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ma_Xiang "Ma Xiang") (馬相) and Zhao Zhi (趙祗) led Yellow Turban remnants to start a rebellion in [Yi Province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yi_Province "Yi Province") (covering present-day [Sichuan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sichuan "Sichuan") and [Chongqing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chongqing "Chongqing")). They killed Li Sheng (李升; Prefect of Mianzhu County 緜竹縣), Zhao Bu (趙部; Administrator of Ba Commandery 巴郡) and Xi Jian (郗儉; Inspector of Yi Province). Ma Xiang declared himself emperor before this sect of the rebellion was suppressed by local forces led by Jia Long (賈龍), a former subordinate of Xi Jian.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-Ma_Xiang,_Xi_Jian,_Zhao_Bu_and_Jia_Long-64)[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-Ma_Xiang_and_Zhao_Zhi-65)

### Xu Province

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Yellow_Turban_Rebellion&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Xu Province")]

In c.November 188, there was a resurgence in Yellow Turban rebels in both Qing and Xu provinces, and they raided numerous counties.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-66) The Yellow Turbans in Xu Province were defeated after Tao Qian was appointed Inspector of the province.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-67)

### Qing Province: Zhang Rao, Guan Hai, Xu He and Sima Ju

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Yellow_Turban_Rebellion&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Qing Province: Zhang Rao, Guan Hai, Xu He and Sima Ju")]

Around 189, Zhang Rao (張饒) led some 200,000 Yellow Turban remnants to ravage [Qing Province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qing_Province "Qing Province"). He defeated imperial forces under [Kong Rong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Rong "Kong Rong"), the Han-appointed Chancellor of [Beihai State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beihai_State "Beihai State") (around present-day [Weifang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weifang "Weifang"), [Shandong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shandong "Shandong")) in Qing Province.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-HHS_70_Zhang_Rao-68) Later, Kong Rong was besieged in Duchang County (都昌縣; present-day [Changyi, Shandong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Changyi,_Shandong "Changyi, Shandong")) by thousands of Yellow Turban rebels led by Guan Hai (管亥). [Taishi Ci](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taishi_Ci "Taishi Ci"), then a military officer under Kong Rong, managed to break out of the siege and seek help from [Liu Bei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liu_Bei "Liu Bei"), who was then the Chancellor of the nearby [Pingyuan State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pingyuan_State "Pingyuan State"). Liu Bei brought along 3,000 troops to attack Guan Hai and succeeded in saving Kong Rong.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-HHS_70_Guan_Hai-69)

In the 200s, Xu He (徐和) and Sima Ju (司馬俱) led Yellow Turban remnants from [Jinan Commandery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jinan_Commandery "Jinan Commandery") (around present-day [Zhangqiu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhangqiu "Zhangqiu"), [Shandong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shandong "Shandong")) and [Le'an Commandery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Le'an_Commandery "Le'an Commandery") (around present-day [Zibo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zibo "Zibo"), Shandong) respectively to ravage [Qing Province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qing_Province "Qing Province"). They were defeated and killed by [Xiahou Yuan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xiahou_Yuan "Xiahou Yuan"), [Zang Ba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zang_Ba "Zang Ba") and Lü Qian some time between 206 and 209.[[f]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-70)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-SGZ_9_Xu_He,_Le'an-71)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-SGZ_18_Xu_He,_Le'an-72)

### Yan Province: Cao Cao's Qingzhou Army

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Yellow_Turban_Rebellion&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Yan Province: Cao Cao's Qingzhou Army")]

Around May 192, hundreds of thousands of Yellow Turban remnants from [Qing Province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qing_Province "Qing Province") swarmed into [Yan Province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yan_Province "Yan Province") and killed Zheng Sui (鄭遂), the Chancellor of Rencheng State (任城國; around present-day [Zoucheng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zoucheng "Zoucheng"), [Shandong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shandong "Shandong")), before moving into Dongping Commandery (東平郡; around present-day [Dongping County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dongping_County "Dongping County"), Shandong). [Liu Dai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liu_Dai "Liu Dai"), the Inspector of Yan Province, wanted to lead his troops to attack the rebels but the general [Bao Xin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bao_Xin "Bao Xin") advised him against it. Liu Dai ignored this advice, dying in his attack against the rebels. Bao Xin and another official, Wan Qian (萬潛), went to Dong Commandery (東郡; around present-day [Puyang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puyang "Puyang"), [Henan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henan "Henan")) to invite [Cao Cao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cao_Cao "Cao Cao") to be the new Governor of Yan Province. Bao Xin then led government forces to attack the rebels at the east of Shouzhang County (壽張縣; south of present-day Dongping County, Shandong) but was killed in action.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-73) Later, despite having fewer troops, Cao Cao managed to defeat the rebels in [Jibei State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jibei_Kingdom "Jibei Kingdom"). The rebels, numbering over 300,000, surrendered to Cao Cao along with their families. Cao Cao then recruited their best warriors and organised them to form an elite military unit, the Qingzhou[[g]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-74) Army (青州兵; also translated as "Qingzhou Corps").[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-75)[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-76)

### Runan and Yingchuan commanderies: He Yi, Liu Pi, Gong Du and others

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Yellow_Turban_Rebellion&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Runan and Yingchuan commanderies: He Yi, Liu Pi, Gong Du and others")]

In Runan Commandery and Yingchuan Commandery, thousands of Yellow Turban remnants remained active under the leadership of He Yi (何儀), Liu Pi (劉辟), Huang Shao (黃邵), and He Man (何曼). They were initially allied with the warlords [Yuan Shu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yuan_Shu "Yuan Shu") and [Sun Jian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sun_Jian "Sun Jian"), but became an independent force in the 190s. Between 17 March and 15 April 196, the warlord [Cao Cao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cao_Cao "Cao Cao") led his forces to attack them and killed Liu Pi, Huang Shao, and He Man. He Yi led the remaining forces in surrendering to Cao Cao.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-He_Yi,_Liu_Pi,_Huang_Shao,_He_Man-77)

Other Yellow Turban forces in Runan Commandery were led by Wu Ba (吳霸) and Gong Du (龔都). Wu Ba was defeated and captured by the general [Li Tong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Li_Tong_(Wenda) "Li Tong (Wenda)").[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-SGZ_18_Wu_Ba-78) Gong Du posed a threat to Cao Cao when he allied with Cao Cao's rival, [Liu Bei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liu_Bei "Liu Bei"), and seized control of Runan Commandery in 201. Cao Cao first sent Cai Yang (蔡揚) to eliminate them, but after Cai Yang was killed, he personally led his troops to attack and defeat them. Liu Bei fled south to join [Liu Biao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liu_Biao "Liu Biao"), while Gong Du and the remaining rebels dispersed.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-Gong_Du-79)

### Yang and Jiao provinces

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Yellow_Turban_Rebellion&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Yang and Jiao provinces")]

Another Yellow Turban remnant force was active in [Kuaiji Commandery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuaiji_Commandery "Kuaiji Commandery") (around present-day [Shaoxing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaoxing "Shaoxing"), [Zhejiang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang "Zhejiang")) until [Liu Zan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liu_Zan "Liu Zan") killed its leader Wu Huan (吳桓).[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-Liu_Zan_and_Wu_Huan-80)

In the 200s, Chen Bai (陳敗) and Wan Cheng (萬秉) started a rebellion in [Jiuzhen Commandery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jiuzhen "Jiuzhen") (九真郡; present-day [Thanh Hóa Province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thanh_H%C3%B3a_Province "Thanh Hóa Province"), [Vietnam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietnam "Vietnam")). In 202, they were defeated and captured by [Zhu Zhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhu_Zhi "Zhu Zhi"), the commandery's administrator.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-Zhu_Zhi,_Chen_Bai,_Wan_Cheng-81)

## Aftermath and impact

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Yellow_Turban_Rebellion&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Aftermath and impact")]

Although the Han armies emerged victorious, the rebellion caused the destruction of major government buildings, deaths of high-ranking officials, and fragmentation of the dynasty's territory. Rebel deaths numbered in the hundreds of thousands, while many non-combatants had been left homeless or destitute by the wars.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-casualties-3) The heavily weakened Han Dynasty was unable to fully govern, distributing its powers to military commanders and local leaders until its complete collapse by 220 AD.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-ANU-8)

After [Emperor Ling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emperor_Ling_of_Han "Emperor Ling of Han") died in 189, a power struggle between his brother-in-law [He Jin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/He_Jin "He Jin") and the eunuchs culminated in He Jin's assassination on 22 September 189. He Jin's chief ally, [Yuan Shao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yuan_Shao "Yuan Shao"), retaliated by setting the palace on fire and slaughtering the eunuchs. The warlord [Dong Zhuo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dong_Zhuo "Dong Zhuo") gained control over the underage heir, [Liu Bian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liu_Bian "Liu Bian"), to legitimize his occupation and ransacking of the capital. Dong Zhuo's reign of terror that followed kicked off a series of [civil wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Campaign_against_Dong_Zhuo "Campaign against Dong Zhuo") and the Three Kingdoms period that lasted for nearly a century.

## In _Romance of the Three Kingdoms_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Yellow_Turban_Rebellion&action=edit&section=24 "Edit section: In Romance of the Three Kingdoms")]

The rebellion is portrayed in the opening chapters of the 14th-century historical novel _[Romance of the Three Kingdoms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romance\_of\_the\_Three\_Kingdoms "Romance of the Three Kingdoms")_, which portrays the Zhang brothers as sorcerers, having been provided the _[Taiping Jing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taiping\_Jing "Taiping Jing")_ from the "[old immortal spirit from the southern lands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xian_(Taoism) "Xian (Taoism)")" (sometimes identified as [Zhuangzi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhuang_Zhou "Zhuang Zhou")).[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Turban_Rebellion#cite_note-roberts-84)

Many fictional Yellow Turban figures were created for the novel, including:

*   [Du Yuan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Du_Yuan "Du Yuan"), killed by [Liao Hua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liao_Hua "Liao Hua") for kidnapping [Liu Bei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liu_Bei "Liu Bei")'s wives
*   [Zhou Cang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhou_Cang "Zhou Cang"), [Guan Yu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guan_Yu "Guan Yu")'s rebel-turned-weapon bearer
*   [Gao Sheng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gao_Sheng_(rebel) "Gao Sheng (rebel)"), a subordinate of Zhang Bao
*   [Cheng Yuanzhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheng_Yuanzhi "Cheng Yuanzhi"), defeated by Liu Bei's forces in their first engagement
*   [Deng Mao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deng_Mao "Deng Mao"), Cheng Yuanzhi's champion
*   [Bian Xi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bian_Xi "Bian Xi"), an eventual servant of [Cao Cao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cao_Cao "Cao Cao") who tried and failed to kill Guan Yu

Though not a fictional character, [Liao Hua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liao_Hua "Liao Hua") was presented in the novel as having been a Yellow Turban rebel in his earlier days, which is historically unlikely, given his date of death and predicted lifespan.

## In popular culture

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Yellow_Turban_Rebellion&action=edit&section=25 "Edit section: In popular culture")]

The rebellion appears as an early stage in each iteration of [Koei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koei "Koei")'s [_Dynasty Warriors_ video game franchise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dynasty_Warriors "Dynasty Warriors"), remaining largely unchanged throughout the series. In [Team Ninja](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Ninja "Team Ninja")'s historical fantasy Action RPG _[Wo Long: Fallen Dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wo\_Long:\_Fallen\_Dynasty "Wo Long: Fallen Dynasty")_, the unnamed player character fights against the rebellion in the first four levels of the game. He Yi, Gong Du, and Huang Shao lead playable factions in the Yellow Turban DLC of the turn-based strategy video game _[Total War: Three Kingdoms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total\_War:\_Three\_Kingdoms "Total War: Three Kingdoms")_, while the Mandate of Heaven DLC features Zhang Jue, Zhang Bao, and Zhang Liang.
